passage:
Friday: Yogesh had been counting days since the letter came. The cousins from Pune were coming Saturday. He cleaned the shelf and set out his carrom board and the building-block set.
Saturday: The cousins tumbled in with bags. Dhruv, the youngest, went straight for the blocks. Yogesh bit his lip, then said, "Take the red ones. I will show you how the bridge goes." Everyone got a turn at carrom, even the little ones.
Sunday: Yogesh caught himself saying, "No, you have to stand here!" Dhruv's face fell. Yogesh stopped, said, "Sorry, you pick the next game," and Dhruv grinned.

qa.q: Where were the cousins coming from?
qa.a: The cousins were coming from Pune.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling on Friday, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He was excited; he had been counting days since the letter came and cleaned the shelf to get ready.

qa.q: What went wrong on Sunday and how did Yogesh fix it?
qa.a: He started ordering Dhruv around and Dhruv's face fell. Yogesh stopped, said sorry and let Dhruv pick the next game.

qa.q: How might Dhruv have felt when Yogesh told Dhruv where to stand?
qa.a: Dhruv probably felt bossed around and a little hurt, since the fun turned into being told what to do until Yogesh apologised.

grounding: A child excited about visiting cousins shares toys and includes everyone, and corrects himself when he starts ordering people around.
